title: Subdivision 328-G — Small business restructure roll-over
summary: A small business entity (or its affiliate, connected entity, or partner) can restructure the ownership of its business assets on a tax-neutral basis under Subdivision 328-G if the transaction is a genuine restructure, does not materially change ultimate economic ownership, all parties meet the small business entity / affiliation / connection / partnership conditions, the assets are active assets, the residency requirement is satisfied, and the parties choose the roll-over. The roll-over cost carries over (s 328-455), pre-CGT status is preserved (s 328-460), new membership interests get a cost base equal to the roll-over costs (s 328-465), capital losses on membership interests affected by the transfer are disregarded (s 328-470), and the Subdivision interacts with Subdivision 152-E small business roll-overs (s 328-475). The safe harbour rule (s 328-435) provides a safe path to satisfy the genuine restructure test. Subsection coverage: operative sections 328-430(1)(a) to (f), 328-430(2), 328-435(a)(b)(c), 328-440(a)(b)(c), 328-445(a)(b)(c)(d), 328-450(1)(a)(b), 328-450(2)(a)(b), 328-455(1)(a)(b), 328-455(2)(a)(b)(c), 328-460, 328-465(1)(a)(b)(c)(d)(e), 328-465(2), 328-470(a)(b)(i)(ii), 328-475(a)(b) mapped to nodes; 328-420, 328-425 (guide); 328-110 (small business entity); 104-10 (CGT event A1); 40-340(1) item 8 (depreciating asset roll-over); 152-E (small business 15-year exemption / retirement roll-over).

nodes.label: A small business entity (or affiliate, connected entity, or partner) transfers business assets to one or more transferees
nodes.body: Subdivision 328-G allows a tax-neutral roll-over when a small business entity restructures its business operations. The transferor transfers a CGT asset (other than a depreciating asset) to one or more transferees. The roll-over is intended to facilitate flexibility for owners of small business entities to restructure how their business assets are held without triggering immediate tax consequences (s 328-425).

nodes.label: Is the transaction a genuine restructure of an ongoing business? (s 328-430(1)(a))
nodes.body: The transaction must be, or be part of, a genuine restructure of an ongoing business. Section 328-435 provides a safe harbour: a transaction is a genuine restructure if, in the 3-year period after the transaction takes effect: (a) there is no change in ultimate economic ownership of any significant assets (other than trading stock) transferred; (b) those significant assets continue to be active assets; and (c) there is no significant or material use of those significant assets for private purposes. The safe harbour does not limit the general meaning of 'genuine restructure' — a transaction may qualify even if it does not meet all three safe harbour conditions.

nodes.label: Does the transaction meet the s 328-435 safe harbour (no change in UEO, assets remain active, no private use)?
nodes.body: The safe harbour is not mandatory — it provides a safe path to satisfy the genuine restructure condition. If met (3-year post-transaction: no UEO change in significant assets other than trading stock; significant assets continue to be active assets; no significant/material private use), the transaction is deemed a genuine restructure. If not met, the transaction may still qualify under the general meaning of genuine restructure.

nodes.label: If safe harbour not met: does the transaction still qualify as a genuine restructure under general principles?
nodes.body: The safe harbour rule (s 328-435) does not limit paragraph 328-430(1)(a). A transaction that does not satisfy the three safe harbour conditions may still be a genuine restructure of an ongoing business. Factors may include business purpose, continuity of business operations, and economic substance. The ATO may examine the surrounding circumstances.

nodes.label: Is each party a small business entity, or does it have an affiliate / connection / partnership that is a small business entity? (s 328-430(1)(b))
nodes.body: Each party to the transfer must satisfy one or more of: (i) it is a small business entity for the income year of the transfer (aggregated turnover < $10M, carrying on business — s 328-110); (ii) it has an affiliate that is a small business entity; (iii) it is connected with an entity that is a small business entity; or (iv) it is a partner in a partnership that is a small business entity. A small business entity must carry on a business in the current year and have aggregated turnover < $10M in the previous year or likely < $10M in the current year (s 328-110(1)).

nodes.label: Does the transaction materially change ultimate economic ownership? (s 328-430(1)(c))
nodes.body: The transaction must not materially change which individual(s) have ultimate economic ownership (UEO) of the asset, or each individual's share of that UEO. For discretionary trusts, s 328-440 provides that a transaction does not change UEO if: the asset was held by a non-fixed family trust before or after the transfer, and every individual with UEO before/after is a member of the same family group (Sch 2F ITAA 1936).

nodes.label: Does the s 328-440 discretionary trust safe harbour apply (asset in a non-fixed family trust, same family group)?
nodes.body: Section 328-440 deems no change in UEO if: (a) just before or just after the transfer, the asset is included in the property of a non-fixed trust that is a family trust; and (b) every individual with UEO just before the transfer was a member of the same family group relating to that trust; and (c) every individual with UEO just after the transfer is also a member of that family group. This safe harbour removes the need to trace ultimate economic ownership through discretionary trust structures.

nodes.label: Is the asset a CGT asset (other than a depreciating asset) that is an active asset? (s 328-430(1)(d))
nodes.body: s 328-430(1)(d): the asset must be a CGT asset (other than a depreciating asset) that is, at the time the transfer takes effect: (i) if the transferor is a small business entity — an active asset; (ii) if the transferor relies on an affiliate/connected entity — an active asset in relation to which s 152-10(1A) is satisfied in that income year, OR WOULD BE SATISFIED IF s 152-10(1AA)(b) WERE DISREGARDED (the statutory alternative); (iii) if the transferor is a partner — an active asset and an interest in an asset of the partnership.

nodes.label: Do the transferor and each transferee meet the residency requirement? (s 328-430(1)(e), s 328-445)
nodes.body: The residency requirement in s 328-445 depends on entity type: (a) individual or company — must be an Australian resident; (b) trust — must be a resident trust for CGT purposes; (c) partnership (other than corporate limited partnership) — at least one partner must be an Australian resident; (d) corporate limited partnership — must be a resident under s 94T ITAA 1936. All parties (transferor and each transferee) must satisfy the requirement.

nodes.label: Is any party an exempt entity or complying superannuation entity? (s 328-430(2))
nodes.body: A roll-over under this Subdivision is not available if the transferor or any transferee is either an exempt entity or a complying superannuation entity. This is a disqualifying condition that overrides all other conditions.

nodes.label: s 328-450: Transfer has no direct income tax consequences
nodes.body: Except as provided by this Subdivision, a transfer of an asset under a roll-over transaction has no direct consequences under the income tax law. For example, if the transfer were from a company to a shareholder, it would not be treated as a deemed dividend under Div 7A ITAA 1936. However, this does not affect the application of income tax law in relation to: (a) anything that happens that does not directly relate to the transfer; or (b) the ownership of the asset at any time.

statute.title: Small business transfers not to affect income tax positions

nodes.label: s 328-455: Assets transferred at roll-over cost (cost base carries over)
nodes.body: Section 328-455(1): Income tax law applies as if the transfer takes place for the asset's roll-over cost. The roll-over cost is (s 328-455(2)): (a) for a CGT asset (other than trading stock, revenue asset or depreciating asset) — the transferor's cost base just before the transfer; (b) for trading stock — the cost of the item to the transferor, or its value at start of the income year if held as trading stock then; (c) for a revenue asset — the amount that would give the transferor no profit or loss on the transfer. This effectively defers any gain/loss by carrying the cost base forward to the transferee.

statute.title: Effect of small business restructures on transferred cost of assets

nodes.label: s 328-460: Pre-CGT assets — transferee taken to have acquired before 20 September 1985
nodes.body: For the purposes of applying s 328-455(1) to a CGT asset (other than a revenue asset) that is a pre-CGT asset, the transferee is taken to have acquired the asset before 20 September 1985. This preserves the pre-CGT status of assets even after the restructure, so that any future capital gain on disposal by the transferee may be disregarded under the pre-CGT exemption.

statute.title: Effect of small business restructures on acquisition times of pre-CGT assets

nodes.label: s 328-465: New membership interests — cost base = roll-over costs ÷ number of interests
nodes.body: If the transaction provides for membership interests to be issued as consideration: the first element of the cost base of each membership interest = (sum of roll-over costs of transferred assets that are neither depreciating assets nor pre-CGT assets + adjustable values of depreciating assets, less liabilities assumed by a transferee) ÷ number of membership interests (s 328-465(1)(d)). The first element of the reduced cost base is worked out similarly. If membership interests are only part of the consideration, these amounts are reduced proportionally (s 328-465(2)).

nodes.label: s 328-470: Capital loss on membership interests affected by transfer is disregarded
nodes.body: If s 328-455 applies to the transfer and an entity holds a membership interest in the transferor or a transferee (or a membership interest issued under the transaction), any capital loss from a CGT event arising in relation to that membership interest after the transaction takes effect is disregarded — except to the extent the entity can demonstrate the loss is attributable to a matter other than the transaction. This prevents taxpayers from engineering artificial capital losses through the restructure.

statute.title: Membership interests affected by transfers of assets

nodes.label: s 328-475: Interaction with Subdivision 152-E small business roll-over (replacement asset)
nodes.body: If the transferor has previously chosen a Subdivision 152-E small business roll-over for a CGT event and the transferred asset is a replacement asset (within the meaning of ss 104-185, 104-190, 104-197, 104-198), then those sections (CGT events J2, J5, J6) apply to each transferee as if the transferee, not the transferor, made the Subdivision 152-E choice. This ensures the deferred gain from the earlier small business roll-over is tracked through to the new entity.

nodes.label: Interaction: Alternative roll-over paths (Div 122-A, 124-M, 615)
nodes.body: Subdivision 328-G is not the only roll-over for business restructures. Alternative paths include: Division 122-A (disposal to wholly-owned company), Subdivision 124-M (scrip for scrip roll-over), and Division 615 (interposed company roll-over). Each has different eligibility conditions. Subdivision 328-G is broader in some respects (works with trusts, partnerships, and entities that are affiliates/connected) but requires the genuine restructure condition and small business entity status.

nodes.label: Interaction: Depreciating assets — s 40-340(1) item 8 roll-over
nodes.body: The CGT asset condition (s 328-430(1)(d)) expressly excludes depreciating assets. Depreciating assets transferred in a small business restructure are dealt with under item 8 of the table in s 40-340(1), which provides a separate roll-over for depreciating assets in the context of small business restructures. Tax-neutral transfer of the depreciating asset at its adjustable value.

nodes.label: Roll-over applies — tax-neutral restructure of small business assets
nodes.body: The Subdivision 328-G roll-over achieves tax neutrality: (1) s 328-450: no direct income tax consequences from the transfer; (2) s 328-455: assets are treated as transferred at roll-over cost (cost base carries over); (3) s 328-460: pre-CGT assets retain pre-CGT status in the transferee's hands; (4) s 328-465: new membership interests receive a cost base reflecting the roll-over costs; (5) s 328-470: capital losses on membership interests affected by the transfer are disregarded; (6) s 328-475: prior Subdivision 152-E roll-over obligations pass to the transferee. The CGT is deferred, not exempted — the transferee steps into the transferor's cost base position.

nodes.label: No roll-over — CGT event A1 applies normally (or alternative roll-overs)
nodes.body: Roll-over not available: the failure conditions include not a genuine restructure, safe harbour not met, no party a small business entity, material change in ultimate economic ownership, non-active asset, residency requirement not met, or a disqualifying exempt entity. CGT event A1 applies normally; alternative roll-over paths may still be available.
